name: Kiribati
summary_text: Kiribati is dangerous for trans visitors. Male same-sex conduct criminalised (14 years, unenforced); no LGR; tiny, isolated, church-dominated society with no visible community infrastructure.

sources.claim_summary: ILGA World Database jurisdiction page for Kiribati: documents the legal status — male same-sex conduct criminalised under colonial-era provisions.

sources.title: Human Dignity Trust
sources.claim_summary: NOTE: Only the Human Dignity Trust homepage was retrievable at fetch time (no Kiribati-specific page); the Trust maps jurisdictions criminalising LGBT people, which include Kiribati.

sources.title: Human rights in Oceania -- lots of work to do
sources.claim_summary: Erasing 76 Crimes (May 2016): excerpts from the 2015 US State Department Country Reports on LGBTI-focused human rights in seven Pacific countries that still criminalise same-sex intimacy - Kiribati among them.

sources.title: Introduction - Gender Identity and Sexual Identity in the Pacific and Hawai'i - Research Guides at University of Hawaii at Manoa
sources.claim_summary: University of Hawaii Manoa library research guide on Pacific sexual identity - resources on sexual and gender diversity across the Pacific, relevant to Kiribati's cultural context.

sources.title: Focus on anti-LGBTI stance of Kuwait, Kiribati
sources.claim_summary: Erasing 76 Crimes (Aug 2015): UPR focus on Kuwait and Kiribati - both urged to improve treatment of LGBTI citizens during the 21st UPR session; documents the recommendations each received.

sources.title: Anti-LGBTI push at U.N. falls short
sources.claim_summary: Erasing 76 Crimes (Nov 2016): the UN General Assembly rejected the plan to undo the SOGI Independent Expert mandate (84-77) - notably Kiribati, despite having an anti-homosexuality law, voted to support the LGBTI rapporteur.
